title: Modernize CI executor profiles and centralize lint/test runners
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our CI pipelines have grown slow and brittle due to heterogeneous executor images, duplicated lint/toolchain installs across repositories, and frequent cache misses. This increases developer feedback time and contributes to flakey PRs (timeouts, transient version skew).

Goal: Reduce median pipeline time by 30% for PRs that run lint + unit tests, cut repeated toolchain installation in half, and improve reproducibility by standardizing executor profiles. We will centralize lint/test runners into a small fleet of pre-baked executor images and introduce explicit executor profiles (tiny, standard, heavy) with clear semantics for CPU, memory, and ephemeral filesystem warmup. A remote install artifact cache and a short-lived cache-priming step will boost cold-starts.

High-level approach:
- Define three canonical executor profiles and document when to use each.
- Build and publish language-shim OCI images containing pinned toolchains (node, python, go, rust) with a lightweight entrypoint that pulls repo code.
- Centralize lint/test execution into a single pipeline template that uses the language-shim images to avoid re-installing dev deps across jobs.
- Add a remote content-addressed install cache (s3-backed with TTL) for pip/npm/cargo artifacts and teach runners to restore/cache using an install-manifest hash.
- Add a short cache-priming job in mainline that warms popular artifact keys on new image rollout.
- Add observability: per-job cache-hit-rate, boot time, toolchain mismatch errors, and median runtime by profile.

Out of scope: Replacing CI provider, migrating to Bazel. This is an incremental modernization focused on build artifact caching and executor consolidation.
acceptance_criteria: Three executor profiles published and documented with sizing guidance
Central lint/test template adopted by at least 60% of active service repos (tracked by adoption dashboard)
Median PR pipeline time for lint+unit tests reduced by >=30% in the first month after rollout
Cache hit rate for install artifacts >= 65% for rolling 7-day window
tasks: Design executor profiles and resource limits (tiny/standard/heavy)
Produce language-shim OCI images for node/python/go/rust and publish in internal registry
Implement remote install cache service and keying strategy (install-manifest hashing)
Create central lint/test pipeline template and migration guide for repos
Add cache-priming job to mainline image release flow
Instrument CI to emit cache-hit-rate, boot-time, and job-runtime metrics
Run migration pilot with 8 non-critical repos and gather perf data
Create rollback plan and canary gating for image rollouts
notes: Proto: used a small pilot on infra/infra-kit and saw cold-start drop from 42s to 18s when image contained cached pip wheel store
We will reuse parts of the buildstamp logic developed in ENG-121345 for image immutability and rotation
Security: language-shim images must be scanned by the scanner pipeline before release; images are immutable and rotate on CVE windows
Registry: store images in ghcr.redwood-inference.internal with :stable and :rolling tags for canary
